prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop web-app UI mockup for an existing personal finance product named “Budget Planner”. This is a dashboard screenshot, not a marketing page, poster, infographic, or mobile app. Landscape desktop canvas around 1536×1024.

DESIGN WORLD
- Minimalist, precise, mature financial tool.
- White and very light neutral canvas; near-black typography; cool-gray hairline dividers.
- Restrained semantic green, amber, and red only for financial status and trend edges.
- No gradients, glassmorphism, purple/teal brand palette, 3D objects, illustrations, photos, shadows everywhere, nested card grids, giant bubbly rounding, or decorative motion.
- Use a clean workhorse sans-serif similar to Geist/Inter, and tabular or monospaced numerals for money.
- Subtle 8–10px radii. Open space and alignment carry the hierarchy.
- Keep a familiar narrow left application sidebar and compact top header. Sidebar items: Dashboard, Transactions, Accounts, Budgets, Goals, Reports. Dashboard is active.
- Use synthetic Philippine peso demo data and show a subtle “Demo data” label. Never include a personal name.

CONCEPT: HEALTH LEDGER
The dashboard should read as one coherent financial diagnosis, not a collection of unrelated widgets. Build a wide main column with a decisive verdict at the top, followed by five aligned health rows. Each row must line up four things: pillar name/question, score/grade, short evidence, and a concrete next action. Borrow the scanability discipline of a fixed-column departures board without copying its visual theme or adding animation. Confine strong color to small status rules, score marks, and trend deltas.

HEADER
- Page title: “Dashboard”
- Compact period control: “This month”
- Compact quick actions at upper right: Add income, Add expense, Transfer, Pay debt

TOP VERDICT
- Large “58 / 100” with status “Needs Attention”
- Blunt headline: “Your finances are held together with duct tape and denial.”
- Supporting line: “Cash flow is the leak. Fix it before it becomes the lifestyle.”
- Small comparison: “Down 4 points from last month”
- One primary action button: “Review spending leaks”

FIVE HEALTH LEDGER ROWS
1. Solvency — “Can you cover what you owe?” — 80, B — “Assets cover liabilities 3.9×” — action “Keep the buffer”
2. Liquidity — “Can you survive an emergency?” — 60, C — “2.4 months of runway” — action “Build one more month”
3. Savings — “Are you keeping enough of what you earn?” — 60, C — “16.6% kept this month” — action “Raise auto-save”
4. Debt Management — “Is your debt under control?” — 60, C — “42% credit utilization” — action “Pay down ₱12,000”
5. Cash Flow — “Is more coming in than going out?” — 40, D — “₱13,600 surplus, shrinking” — action “Cut top 3 leaks”
Make these mostly row-based with dividers, not five floating cards.

LOWER OPERATING AREA
- A clean 6-month income vs expense line/bar chart titled “Cash flow trend”
- Compact evidence strip: Net worth ₱284,500; Income ₱82,000; Expenses ₱68,400; Surplus ₱13,600
- A budget progress section: “76% used” and top categories Housing, Food, Transport, with clear progress bars
- Accounts/debt summary: Cash ₱176,000; Debt ₱96,000; Net worth ₱284,500
- Recent transactions table with 4 rows, concise merchants and amounts
Avoid a permanent AI teaser, account carousel, invoice carousel, achievement confetti, or decorative charts.

The screen should feel calm but not dull: decisive copy, excellent information hierarchy, varied density, thin rules, and a few sharp semantic accents. Ensure the UI remains legible and plausible as a real Next.js/shadcn dashboard.
